title: Small Mayer-Vietoris endpoint families
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes in universe $u$, let $U,V$ be opens of $X$, and let $f:Y\to X$ be an open immersion with image $U\cup V$. Suppose $P_w(X,U)$, $P_w(X,V)$, and $P_w(X,U\cap V)$ [def-pc-perfect-classes-small-on-open]. Fix derived categories in morphism universe $w$ on $Y$ and its localized open sites [def-pc-derived-category]. Then the skeletons of both endpoint families $M_{f^{-1}U,f^{-1}V}$ and $N_{f^{-1}U,f^{-1}V}$ [def-perfect-gluing-endpoint-properties] are $u$-small.

source.place: Tag 08BV, lemma-exact-sequence-j-star; Step 2 of lem-pc-perfect-complexes-compact-set, using Tag 08DR

proof.text: U,V and U intersect V lie in opensRange f. Apply the restriction-smallness theorem to each; preimage preserves intersections.

Index middle endpoints by the product of the first two restriction skeletons and overlap endpoints by the third restriction skeleton. Send a skeleton representative through the actual derived direct-image functor, taking the biproduct for middle endpoints. Any endpoint in the property is isomorphic to such an image by fromSkeletonToSkeletonIso, mapped by direct image and biproduct.mapIso.

For any small family of ambient objects covering a full subcategory up to isomorphism, map its skeleton injectively into the range of the family in the ambient skeleton. Full faithfulness gives mapSkeleton_injective, and small_of_injective gives smallness. Apply this proved private helper to the two constructed families.
